messages.author: 2f3428d3166aad1c
messages.subject: Re: datadr
parts:
Yes - for a tutorial with some toy examples, please see:

http://tesseradata.github.io/docs-datadr/

For a better illustration of using the tools on more real-life problems, see here:

http://tesseradata.github.io/example-vast-challenge/

These docs are undergoing a lot of change right now, but they should be good for the most part.

Also, I am working on a quickstart script that quickly gives a feel for a few of the possible operations you can do.  Here's an example of some code to run:

# quick start for local usage of datadr / trelliscope

# install packages
library(devtools)
install_github("datar", "tesseradata")
install_github("trelliscope", "tesseradata")


library(datadr)
library(trelliscope)

# express barley data as a local "distributed data frame"
barleyDdf <- ddf(barley)

# divide the ddf by the variable "site"
bySite <- divide(barleyDdf, by = "site")

# look at the ddf object
bySite

# look at subsets of the ddf
bySite[[1]]
bySite[["site=Grand Rapids"]]

# compute mean yield for each subset and recombine with "rbind"
recombine(bySite,
   apply = function(x) mean(x$yield),
   combine = combRbind())

## make a simple trelliscope display on this division

# initialize visualization database (vdb) connection
vdbConn("vdb", autoYes = TRUE)

# simple dotplot panel function
pf <- function(x)
   dotplot(variety ~ yield, data = x)
# test it on a subset
pf(bySite[[1]][[2]])

# simple cognostics function
cf <- function(x) {
   list(
      meanYield = cogMean(x$yield, desc = "mean yield"),
      range = cogRange(x$yield, desc = "yield range"),
      min = cog(min(x$yield), desc = "min yield"),
      max = cog(max(x$yield), desc = "min yield")
   )
}
# test it on a subset
cf(bySite[[1]][[2]])

# add display with this panel and cognostics function to vdb 
makeDisplay(bySite,
   name = "variety_vs_yield",
   desc = "test display with barley data",
   panelFn = pf, cogFn = cf,
   width = 400, height = 400,
   lims = list(x = "same", y = "free")
)

# view the display
view()
